newsitem.title: USA: Epitope down on strawberry scare.
newsitem.headline: Epitope down on strawberry scare.

text.p: Shares of Epitope Inc continued to lose ground Thursday in the aftermath of disclosures that frozen strawberries it distributed were tainted with the hepatitis-A virus.

But the company was slow to discuss what effect the incident would have on its financial performance, saying it first needed to recall the fruit and see that children and others who ate it were inoculated.
While the drop was linked to the hepatitis scare, analysts noted the company's outlook had been weak even before that.

"It's just the continuation of a dismal story," said Evan Sturza, analyst with Sturza's Institutional Research. Sturza said he has had a "sell" rating on Epitope for some time, based on the poor performance of its two units: the agricultural operation, which distributed the strawberries; and the diagnostic unit, which makes an HIV test.
Epitope acquired the agricultural unit as a way to offset losses and weak sales at its diagnostic business.

Analysts also said that product liability insurance would likely cover the costs of recalling the tainted fruit, but a longer term challange for the company would be winning back the trust of consumers.
In addition, there were reports the company could face criminal charges if it were found to have imported the strawberries from Mexico, in violation of U.S. law.
